title: DOR/ISL in Pediatric Participants With HIV-1, <18 Years of Age and ≥ 35 kg
official: A Phase 2 Clinical Study to Evaluate the Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Efficacy of Oral Doravirine/Islatravir (100 mg/0.25 mg) in Pediatric Participants With HIV-1 Infection Who Are Virologically Suppressed or Treatment-Naïve, Are Less Than 18 Years of Age, and Weigh Greater Than or Equal to 35 kg
summary:
This is a phase 2 study of the pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy of oral doravirine/islatravir (100 mg/0.25 mg) \[MK-8591A\] in pediatric participants with human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection who are virologically suppressed or treatment-naive.

The Base Study will last from Day 1 to Week 96. At Week 96, participants will be given the option to participate in an optional Study Extension and receive DOR/ISL until Week 240 or until it becomes commercially accessible, whichever is first.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Pediatric participant with HIV-1 \<18 years of age
* Body weight ≥35 kg
* Is TN (HIV-1 positive with plasma HIV-1 RNA ≥500 copies/mL) or VS (HIV-1 positive at screening with plasma HIV-1 RNA \<50 copies/mL AND has received stable, continuous 2- or 3-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) for ≥3 months prior to providing informed consent)

Exclusion Criteria:

* HIV-2 infection
* Hypsensitivity/contraindication to any components of study medication or as determined by the investigator
* Has an active diagnosis of hepatitis due to any cause
* history of malignancy ≤5 years prior to signing informed consent except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, in situ cervical cancer, or cutaneous Kaposi's sarcoma
* Has a history or current evidence of any condition (including active tuberculosis infection, COVID-19, or other infections), therapy, laboratory abnormality, or other circumstance (including drug or alcohol use or dependence) that might, in the opinion of the investigator, confound the results of the study
* Is taking or is anticipated to require systemic immunosuppressive therapy, immune modulators, or any prohibited therapies
